rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken word for a physical cavity, pit, dent, or opening through something.

example.english: There’s a hole in the sneaker.
example.jyutping: go3 bo1 haai4 cyun1 zo2 go3 lung1

rows.note: Use this for a flaw, gap, or loophole in an argument, plan, or system rather than a literal opening.

example.english: This plan has a hole in it, so people will definitely catch it.
example.traditional: 呢個計劃有個漏洞，實畀人捉到㗎。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 gai3 waak6 jau5 go3 lau6 dung6 sat6 bei2 jan4 zuk3 dou2 gaa3

rows.note: Use this when “a hole” means being in serious difficulty, especially financial trouble.

example.english: He owes so much money that he’s gotten himself into a hole.
example.traditional: 佢欠咗咁多錢，搞到自己陷入困境。
example.jyutping: keoi5 him3 zo2 gam3 do1 cin2 gaau2 dou3 zi6 gei2 haam6 jap6 kwan3 ging2

rows.note: Use this ordinary body-part noun for the mouth, including in expressions referring rudely to someone's mouth.

example.traditional: 收聲啦，你個口真係好煩呀！
example.jyutping: sau1 seng1 laa1 nei5 go3 hau2 zan1 hai6 hou2 faan4 aa3
